tip: нельзя (nelzya = not allowed) puts the person in the dative: детям нельзя (detyam nelzya = children may not). There is no verb 'to be'.
с (s) means 'with' and takes the instrumental: с вами (s vami = with you). The verb познакомиться (paznakomitsya = get acquainted) normally pairs with с.
A few masculine nouns take a stressed -у in the locative: в саду (v sadu = in the garden), not в саде (v sade). Same for в лесу (v lesu), на мосту (na mastu).
For games, use играть в (igrat v = play) plus the accusative: играет в шахматы (igrayet v shakhmaty = plays chess). Instruments take играть на (igrat na).
кроме (krome = besides) takes the genitive: кроме тебя (krome tebya = besides you).
из (iz = out of) takes the genitive and matches the вы- (vy-) prefix: вышел из дома (vyshel iz doma = went out of the house).
к (k = toward) takes the dative: подошёл к окну (padashyol k aknu = came up to the window).
из-за (iz-za = because of) takes the genitive and marks a negative cause: из-за дождя (iz-za dazhdya = because of the rain).
нужен (nuzhen) agrees with the needed noun, not the person: прогулка (pragulka, feminine) takes нужна (nuzhna = is needed).
The one who likes goes dative: коту (katu = to the cat). The verb agrees with the liked thing: нравится (nravitsya = likes, singular).
стать (stat' = to become) takes the instrumental: стала учительницей (stala uchitel'nitsey = became a teacher).
друг другу (drug drugu = each other) is fixed; only the second word shifts case, here dative after помогают (pamagayut = help).
Difficulty puts the person in the dative with no subject 'it': мне трудно (mne trudna = it is hard for me).
бывает (byvaet = tends to be) marks a recurring trait and takes an instrumental complement: холодной (khalodnoy = cold).
нечего (nechevo) plus an infinitive means having nothing to: нечего надеть (nechevo nadet' = nothing to wear); the person goes dative, мне (mne).
Russian places things with posture verbs: стол стоит (stol stait = the table stands), not a plain 'is'.
между (mezhdu = between) takes the instrumental: между друзьями (mezhdu druz'yami = between friends).
среди (sredi = among) takes the genitive: среди гостей (sredi gastey = among the guests).
из also means made of, with the genitive: букет из роз (buket iz roz = a bouquet of roses).
The receiver goes in the dative: маме (mame = to mom). The gift цветы (tsvety = flowers) stays the direct object.
After стал (stal = became), the new role goes in the instrumental: известным врачом (izvestnym vrachom = a famous doctor).
The verb гордимся (gardimsya = we are proud) takes the instrumental with no preposition: нашими детьми (nashimi det'mi = our children).
с (s = with) takes the instrumental: с грибами (s gribami = with mushrooms), naming what the soup is made with.
о (o = about) takes the prepositional case: о своём детстве (o svayom detstve = about her childhood).
требует (trebuyet = requires) takes the genitive, not the accusative: большого терпения (bal'shova terpeniya = great patience).
This masculine noun takes a stressed -у for location: в углу (v uglu = in the corner), not the usual -е ending.
за (za = behind) takes the instrumental for a static location: за забором (za zaborom = behind the fence).
With no stated subject, the plural verb подарили (padarili = they gave) reads as a passive, was given, the normal Russian pattern.
понравилась (panravilas', feminine) agrees with презентация (prezentatsiya = presentation), the thing liked, not with коллегам (kallegam = colleagues).
The tool used takes the instrumental with no preposition: ложкой (lozhkoy = with a spoon).
